output:
Tree is clean, my probe files are removed. Here's the review.

---

# Review — `base..HEAD` (`fix: align peg alert history and Slack links`)

**Target pinned:** detached HEAD `5e984549`, one commit ahead of local branch `base` (`d2360261`). 9 files, 331+/59−, **~211 non-test lines**. Working tree clean apart from untracked `.skill/`. Reviewed the whole commit as one unit.

**Second model:** ran `~/.claude/bin/codex-review.sh base` (gpt-5.6-sol @ high) as the tooling reference requires. It independently found #1, #2 and #6; it missed #3 and #4. Its findings below are re-verified against the real code, not relayed. `~/.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview` does not exist on this machine.

**Verdict: does not pass.** Four must-fixes, one of them a confirmed CI failure.

---

## Fix before merge

**1. `terraform test` fails — the required PR gate cannot pass**
`alerts/rules/peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69`

The assertion requires `peg_slack_title` to contain `$alert.Annotations.summary` and `$alert.Annotations.resolved_summary`. `peg-message-templates.tf:13-17` removed both when it reduced the title to a status icon. The JS mirror (`scripts/alerts/alert-rules-lint.test.mjs:1255-1269`) *was* updated; this Terraform sibling was not.

> **Confirmed by execution.** I ran `terraform init -backend=false && terraform test` in `alerts/rules`: `Failure! 0 passed, 1 failed` — *"Peg Slack copy must lead with the cause and leave state to the title icon."* `ci.yml:874-879` runs this on every pull request; `alerts-rules.yml:254` runs it on push.

Fix: update the assertion to require an icon-only title and require the linked summaries in `peg_slack_message` — mirroring what the `.mjs` lint now asserts.

---

**2. A recovered rule shows "Monitoring failed" forever**
`ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/peg-alert-events.ts:105-115`, `route.ts:43-56`

For a rule with a non-zero `for` period, Grafana recovers `Error → Pending → Alerting`, not `Error → Alerting`. That `Error → Pending` row is neither fetched (`errorStateHistoryUrl` only produces `current=Error` and `previous=Error&current=Normal`) nor classified (`transitionKind` returns `null` when `current` is `Pending`). The error cycle opened at `Normal → Error` never closes, so `pairStateTransitions:356` flushes it as a bare, permanently-unresolved event.

Non-zero `for_duration` is common in these rules — `peg-rule-definitions.tf:75, 97, 232, 254, 370, 392`.

> **Confirmed empirically.** Feeding `Normal→Error`, `Pending→Alerting`, `Alerting→Normal` through `combinePegAlertEvents` yields:
> ```
> cleared | Bitvavo buy and sell prices were 34 bps apart | EUROP · lasted 50 min.
> warning | Bitvavo buy and sell prices are 34 bps apart  | EUROP.
> warning | Grafana could not evaluate the Bitvavo Peg rule | EUROP.   ← never recovers
> ```
> The Grafana-side claim that `Error → Pending` is the real transition shape is from documented state-machine behaviour — **not verified against your deployed Grafana Cloud version.** Worth confirming before picking the fix.

Fix: query `previous=Error` without constraining `current`, and classify `Error → Pending` as recovery.

---

**3. Incidents that start from an Error lose "lasted X" on resolution**
`ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/peg-alert-events.ts:320-321` (with `:109-110`)

`cycleKey` routes any kind starting with `"error"` to the `error` cycle. So `Error → Alerting`, which base classified as `"raised"`, now only closes the error cycle and never opens the alert cycle. The later `Alerting → Normal` finds nothing open, falls through to `unpairedCleared`, and is emitted with no duration.

> **Confirmed by A/B execution.** Same three transitions, base vs. HEAD:
> ```
> base:  cleared | ...were 34 bps apart | EUROP · lasted 10 min.
> HEAD:  cleared | ...were 34 bps apart | EUROP.
> ```
> The incident duration — the one number an operator scans this panel for — is silently dropped.

Fix: have `error-recovered-alerting` open the alert cycle as well as close the error cycle (emit both transitions from that row).

---

**4. Two supplementary queries are now hard dependencies of the whole panel**
`ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/route.ts:63-83`

`fetchJson` went from one request to two, and `GET:115-118` calls it twice — four upstream calls where there were two, all inside a `Promise.all` that rejects on first failure. `route.ts:126-133` maps any rejection to 502/504, and the client renders *"Recent alerts unavailable."*

So if the deployed Grafana rejects `current=Error` or `previous=Error` — or either new call transiently 500s or times out — the **entire seven-day peg alert history disappears**, to protect a supplementary feature. That the new query shapes are unverified against live Grafana (see #2) is exactly why this should fail open.

> Confirmed by reading; the *trigger* is unverified. Fix is small: let the error-history request resolve to `[]` on failure rather than rejecting the batch.

---

## Follow-up, not blocking

**5. Source-less rules are attributed to a "Price source" that doesn't exist** — `peg-alert-events.ts:230`
`evaluationCause` always calls `pegAlertSourceName`, which returns the literal `"Price source"` for an empty source (`peg-alert-copy.ts:47-49`). Seven rules set `source = ""` (`peg-rule-definitions.tf:102, 215, 281, 397, 510, 576, 600`). Confirmed empirically: a structural-saturation failure renders *"Grafana could not evaluate the Price source Peg rule"*, sending on-call to check price feeds for a rule that has none. The pre-existing `pegAlertCauseCopy` path handles these rules correctly — only the new copy is affected.

**6. Canonical note now contradicts the code** — `docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:118`, `:132-133`
Line 118 says *"Slack titles use the severity icon plus that summary"* — the summary is gone. Lines 132-133 say the backend *"reads only fired and resolved transitions… does not read Pending or canceled transitions"* — it now reads Error transitions too. Both confirmed by reading.

**7. Monitoring-failure entries compete for the four visible slots** — `route.ts:22`
`PEG_ALERTS_MAX_EVENTS = 4`, and each error cycle emits **two** events (failed + recovered). One flapping datasource fills half the panel; two fill it entirely, pushing real peg breaches out of view. Consider capping evaluation-state events separately.

**8. Response byte cap is now per-request** — `route.ts:80`
`PEG_ALERTS_MAX_STATE_RESPONSE_BYTES` (4 MiB) is enforced inside the per-URL map, so a single `GET` can now buffer up to 16 MiB instead of 8 MiB.

## Handed back to you

**Icon-only Slack title.** The code comment states the rationale (Grafana hardcodes `title_link`), and the title now renders as exactly one emoji — I verified the trim markers produce no stray whitespace. But the attachment title is what Slack shows in mobile push notifications and channel previews, so a page now previews as `🚨` with no cause. That's a real on-call ergonomics trade, and it's your call, not something the diff can settle.

---

## Considered and discarded

- **Slack link injection via `{{ . }}`** — summary annotations contain no `<`, `>`, or `|`; checked `peg-copy-locals.tf`. Link syntax is safe.
- **New title template whitespace** — `{{ define … -}}` / `{{- end }}` trim correctly; the rendered template printed by `terraform test` confirms a bare icon.
- **Client rejecting the new field** — `use-peg-alerts.ts` casts the response with no runtime schema, so optional `evaluationState` can't be rejected. No `.strict()` validator anywhere on this path.
- **`RULE_EXPLANATIONS[rule]` blowing up on evaluation events** — the early returns at `peg-alert-explanation.ts:294-302` cover all three states before the lookup at `:304`.
- **`error-recovered-alerting` being a dead branch** — it isn't; those rows arrive via the pre-existing `current=Alerting` query, not via `errorStateHistoryUrl`.
- **Hardcoded `monitoring.mento.org`** — matches existing convention (`contact-points.tf:231`), not a regression.
- **Green checks:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; the two touched vitest suites pass (60 tests); `alerts:rules:lint` and its 50-test suite pass. None of that exercises #2, #3 or #4 — the new tests cover `Error → Normal` and `Error → Alerting` in isolation, never the sequences that break.

## What I could not do

- No live Grafana. The `current=Error` and `previous=Error` filters, and the `Error → Pending` transition shape, are **unverified against your deployed version** — findings #2 and #4 both hinge on this.
- Did not run the full `ui-dashboard` suite myself (codex reported 4,385 passing; I ran the two targeted suites plus typecheck and the alert linter).
- No browser verification of the new history rows, and no real Slack delivery to check the icon-only title.
- `terraform plan` not run (no credentials) — only `terraform test`.

## Proof still owed

Re-run `terraform test` after fixing the assertion; exercise the endpoint against real Grafana to confirm both new query shapes are accepted and to pin the actual `Error →` recovery path; add a browser fixture rendering a monitoring-failure row; send one real Slack notification. A clean read here is not a release gate — your normal pre-push checks still apply.
other_review:
The patch breaks a required Terraform test and has reachable Grafana recovery-state defects that can omit recoveries or leave an alert cycle open. It also produces incorrect copy for source-less rules and contains several ineffective regression tests.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Update the Terraform test for icon-only titles — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/alerts/rules/peg-message-templates.tf:14-14
  The required Terraform test still asserts that `peg_slack_title` contains both summary annotations in `alerts/rules/peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:66-75`. This icon-only template contains neither, so `terraform test -no-color` will fail in CI. Update the assertion to verify the new icon-only title and linked message-body contract. See `alerts/AGENTS.md:52-55`.

- [P1] Synchronize alert cycles when evaluation recovers — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/peg-alert-events.ts:344-352
  Because error and alert transitions use separate keys, an `Alerting → Error → Normal` sequence closes only the error cycle and leaves the earlier alert cycle open, so Recent alerts still reports an active breach after Grafana returns to Normal. The reverse boundary case also fails: if the window begins with `Error → Alerting`, a later clear has no alert opener and loses its duration. Apply each recovery to the alert cycle as well: close it on Normal and seed it on Alerting.

- [P2] Capture Error-to-Pending recoveries — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/peg-alert-events.ts:109-113
  When a rule with a nonzero `for` duration recovers from `Error` while its condition remains true, Grafana can transition to `Pending`. This classifier handles only recovery to Normal or Alerting, and the companion request filters specifically for `current=Normal`, so the feed retains the failure but omits the recovery. Query bounded transitions with `previous=Error` and classify `Error → Pending` as a monitoring recovery.

- [P2] Identify source-less rules without inventing a price source — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/peg-alert-events.ts:230-234
  Structural, indexed-pool, heartbeat, and policy-rollover rules set `source` to an empty string. `pegAlertSourceName("")` returns `Price source`, so their failures are displayed as “Grafana could not evaluate the Price source Peg rule,” although no price source exists for those rules. Build the subject from the rule and asset or policy when `source` is empty.

- [P2] Keep the canonical Peg runbook aligned — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/alerts/rules/peg-message-templates.tf:13-15
  The canonical runbook still says Slack titles contain the severity icon plus the summary and that history reads only fired and resolved transitions (`docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:116-133`). This patch makes titles icon-only and adds evaluation failures and recoveries. Update both statements so operators do not follow stale behavior. `AGENTS.md:25-27` defines canonical context as current operating truth.

- [P2] Return fresh Response objects from multi-fetch tests — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/__tests__/route.test.ts:817-820
  These three failure tests use one `mockResolvedValue` `Response` for several remaining fetches. A response body can be consumed only once, so a later companion request fails from body reuse and returns 502 regardless of whether the malformed, oversized, or sentinel input was detected correctly. Use a mock factory that returns a fresh `Response` for every fetch at lines 819, 832, and 846.

- [P2] Assert against the actual breach explanation — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/ui-dashboard/src/app/peg-monitoring/__tests__/recent-alerts.test.tsx:190-193
  The negative assertion searches for `sell price is below peg`, but production copy always inserts a provider and measurement, and the breach details use a different explanation sentence. The assertion therefore still passes if the monitoring-failure early return is removed. Assert that the actual movement explanation is absent so this test protects the intended no-breach-copy behavior.

- [P3] Scope Slack assertions to their template resources — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1999-5e9845490149/scripts/alerts/alert-rules-lint.test.mjs:1260-1267
  The link checks search the complete Terraform source, so matching text in another resource can satisfy them even if `peg_slack_message` loses its links. The title slice also does not validate that either resource marker was found. Validate the ordered marker indexes and assert title icons and message links within separately extracted resources so this regression test fails closed.
